system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of the Seller package:** reviewed in full against the Buyer Playbook. Nothing in it is accepted.

## 0. Threshold point – the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" must be disregarded

The Seller's cover note says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny", that only **[OPEN]** items require review, and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package".

That is not correct and we should not proceed on that basis:

- No clause in the package has been cleared by us. Our playbook has no agreed positions on any of them, and the two items on which a fallback exists (20% cap; 18-month claims period) expressly require Amelia Frost's prior written authority, which has not been given.
- Every substantive clause is marked [STANDARD]; nothing is marked [OPEN]. Taken at face value the note would have us review nothing.
- The note is the other side's framing of the negotiation, not an agreed record. It should be treated as a negotiating tactic (or a drafting attempt to manufacture an "agreed" baseline) and rebutted in writing so there is no later argument of acquiescence.

**Recommendation:** respond that all provisions remain open, that no limitation or disclosure framework has been accepted, and that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels have no agreed status.

---

## 1. Clause-by-clause departures from the Playbook

| # | Clause / topic | Seller position | Playbook position | Gap / risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.1 General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with Frost written authority | Seller has opened at our *conditional* fallback. Do not concede. |
| 2 | 12.2 Thresholds | De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; **excess-only** recovery | De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; **first-dollar** recovery | 5× on both thresholds plus a tipping→deductible switch. Deductible alone costs us AUD 250k on every claim profile. |
| 3 | 12.3 / 13 Claims period | 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | 24 months; 18 only with Frost approval | Second sentence is a hidden general-regime override that would drag Fundamental, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claims into the 18-month/20% regime. Delete. |
| 4 | Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Unacceptable. Title to the shares is the entire consideration; capping it at 20% is not a simplification, it is a transfer of ~AUD 19m of risk. |
| 5 | 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | Apply to **all Claims of any nature** | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | No fraud carve-out at all. This is non-negotiable under the playbook and likely unenforceable as drafted in NSW in any event, but we must not sign it. |
| 6 | Sch 7 Disclosure | General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room / public-register / prudent-search deeming | Whole-data-room disclosure effectively neutralises the warranties. Reject in full; require matters to be disclosed with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope. |
| 7 | 8.3 Buyer knowledge | No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test, extended to advisers. Combined with item 6 it leaves almost nothing claimable. Delete. |
| 8 | 3 / 6.3 Bluefen consent (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent | Effective consent **and** evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Disclosure Letter §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction exists. A consent "on delivery" that is itself conditional is no consent. Make this a true Condition Precedent. |
| 9 | 2 / 7 Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release to be provided **after** Completion | Current payout figure; repayment direct from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval | Disclosure §3 confirms facility unpaid and no discharge in data room. Buying a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and only a promise of release is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. |
| 10 | Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k) | "A matter for the Seller", not itemised | Specific line item or seller-funded, **including triggered on-costs** | Disclosure §5 confirms the amounts are not in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax/super. If paid by the Company post-Completion, we fund them. Require an express line item (bonus + on-costs) deducted from the price or paid by Seller. |
| 11 | 11.1 Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified | Under DD-004 cl. 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do **not** transfer until every fee is cleared – a title-to-IP issue, not merely a payment issue. Indemnity must cover loss of/failure to obtain the IP, third-party claims and costs, not just the AUD 180k. Seek bank evidence of payment status and a confirmatory assignment at Completion. |
| 12 | 4.6 / Sch 6 Incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records) | "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" | Preserve logs; investigate; require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Do not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation, and do not overstate it ourselves. Require: log preservation covenant, completion of investigation (or status report) pre-Completion, Privacy Act/OAIC assessment, pre-Completion updates, and a specific indemnity for notification/remediation costs if a breach is later confirmed. |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Ordinary-course operating costs | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Disclosure §8 says nothing about whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Ask the questions; do not pre-commit to treating them as Debt, but do not accept "ordinary course" as a conclusion either. |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed | Not settled. Tax and IP must be in their own regimes (cap, period) and expressly excluded from the general-regime override in cl. 13. |
| 15 | Title evidence | Share register at DD-012 | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal source | The Seller's own Disclosure §10 concedes DD-012 merely "identifies the source relied on". Require ASIC search, PPSR search, Riverlark security discharge (links to item 9), constitution/board/shareholder approvals and a title and capacity warranty in the Fundamental regime. |

## 2. Observations on the Disclosure Letter

The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the SPA Update and is useful to us:

- §2, §3, §5, §10 effectively admit that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonus funding and independent title verification are all *outstanding*. These support making items 8, 9, 10 and 15 Conditions Precedent / Completion deliverables.
- §1.4 (no admission of anything) combined with §1.1–1.2 (disclose everything) is the classic "disclose the whole room, admit nothing" structure. The Letter should be re-cut so that only the numbered specific disclosures (§§2–10) qualify the warranties, and §1.1–1.2 are deleted.
- §7 (office lease – notification only) and §9 (Mossvale – assignment restriction only, not a change-of-control consent) appear on their face to be low-risk, but we should verify the underlying clauses ourselves rather than rely on the Seller's reading.
- §11 is correct that we must evaluate against the full DD record; we should not treat the Letter as closing out any DD workstream.

## 3. Interaction / cumulative risk

Items 1–7 should be read together. In combination they produce a regime in which: (a) nearly every matter is "disclosed" by virtue of being in the data room; (b) anything in the data room is "discoverable" and therefore barred by Buyer knowledge; (c) whatever survives is subject to a AUD 25k/250k deductible, 20% cap and 18-month window; (d) that regime extends to title, tax, IP and fraud. The practical result is a largely warranty-free acquisition. This is the single most important point to make to the Seller – the package is not "fair and balanced", it is structurally one-sided.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Rebut the Efficiency Note in writing.** Nothing is agreed; all clauses remain open; the [STANDARD] label has no status.
2. **Liability regime:** cap 25% / AUD 6.0m; de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k, first-dollar recovery; 24-month general claims period. Delete the cl. 13 "applies to all Claims" override.
3. **Fundamental/Title:** separate regime – 100% cap, minimum 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge qualifiers.
4. **Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct:** express carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-waivable.
5. **Disclosure:** delete general data-room/public-register/registers disclosure (§1.1–1.2); specific fair disclosure only.
6. **Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3):** delete. Any seller-knowledge qualifier to be by named persons after reasonable enquiry only, and never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Condition Precedent requiring effective written consent **plus** evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours is not sufficient.
8. **Riverlark:** current payout letter; repayment from Completion funds via funds flow; executed security releases/PPSR discharges at Completion. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval – not our preferred route.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item (price deduction) or seller-funded; Seller to confirm on-cost position.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to cover failure of IP transfer, third-party claims and costs; keep the SOW3 cure; obtain bank evidence of the AUD 180k status and a confirmatory assignment at Completion.
11. **DD-006 incident:** log-preservation covenant, investigation completion/status, pre-Completion updates, and a specific indemnity if a notifiable breach is confirmed. Take no position on materiality or quantum in either direction.
12. **Sandbar:** issue supplementary DD questions on termination rights, accrual and necessity before deciding treatment; no automatic Debt classification or deduction.
13. **Tax/IP:** record as OPEN with their own cap/period categories; reject "settled under the general regime".
14. **Title:** require independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, authorities, Riverlark release); DD-012 is corroborative only.
15. **Keep all categories separate** (Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenants, specific indemnities) with an express clause that general limitations do not apply to them unless stated.

**Escalations needed to Amelia Frost:** none of the fallbacks (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release) should be offered or accepted without her written authority; at present we hold the primary positions on all three.
=== END ADVICE ===
